title: Controller tests with @WebMvcTest

richText: @WebMvcTest loads Spring MVC components for controller testing. It does not load the whole application.
It can check request mapping, JSON binding, input validation and HTTP responses.
Provide the controller’s service dependencies as mock beans or imported test configuration.
MockMvc sends a request through the configured Spring MVC infrastructure without opening a real network port.
Check the response status, headers and relevant body fields.
Mock the service response when the test is about controller behavior. Test the real service separately.
For Spring Boot 3.4 and later, use @MockitoBean from Spring Framework to replace a collaborator in the test context.
Older Boot 3 examples use @MockBean. It was deprecated in Boot 3.4.
A plain Mockito @Mock field is not a replacement Spring bean.
Include the access rules being checked
Spring Security is included when it is on the classpath. Import the application’s relevant security configuration when checking its rules.
Add spring-security-test for helpers such as @WithMockUser.
@WithMockUser supplies test authentication. It does not test password verification.
Keep security filters enabled when the requirement is an access rule.
For protected POST, PUT or DELETE requests, supply the CSRF token when the application requires it.

summary: Check request mapping and responses without loading the full application.
